name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
description: The single-arm lat pulldown trains each side of the back independently, allowing greater range of motion through freedom of lateral trunk flexion and improved scapular movement. It is particularly useful for identifying and correcting left-to-right strength imbalances in the latissimus dorsi and is an effective finishing exercise after bilateral pulldowns.

execution.starting_position: Attach a single D-handle to a lat pulldown machine or high pulley. Sit or kneel facing the machine and grasp the handle with one hand, arm fully extended overhead.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a D-handle to the high pulley. Sit at the machine or kneel on the floor. Set an appropriate weight — typically less than half the bilateral pulldown weight.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the working arm fully extended, lat on stretch, allowing a slight lateral lean away from the cable.
Step 2: Depress the shoulder blade of the working side and initiate the pull.
Step 3: Drive the elbow down and toward the hip, pulling the handle to the upper chest or shoulder.
Step 4: Squeeze the lat hard at the bottom and pause briefly.
Step 5: Return under control to full extension, letting the lat fully lengthen.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull down. Inhale as you return to start.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso excessively rather than isolating the lat
Using the hand and grip rather than the elbow to initiate the pull
safety_considerations: Keep the core engaged to prevent excessive lateral trunk flexion that shifts load to the spine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead extension to handle at chest/shoulder level. Allow natural lateral trunk movement.
coaching_cues: Imagine trying to put the handle in your front pocket
Let your shoulder reach for the ceiling at the top — full stretch
Drive the elbow, not the hand
